records.supported_name_scope: The three modeled mainstem fragments follow the Berbice corridor. No separately selected tributary or lake passage is identified.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Eastern Guyana: the selected upper Berbice northward route, Duck River junction setting, Kwakwani bend and lower New Amsterdam–Rosignol corridor distinguish the selection from Essequibo, Demerara, Canje and Corentyne.
records.completion_scope: Complete regional-scale correspondence review of all three selected pieces against readable original cartography. Generalization leaves fine channel positions and exact naming boundaries unresolved, without a regional connection or coverage gap.

naming_scope_details.distinct_selected_upstream_route: Upper Berbice corridor; no separate initial feeder hydronym established.
naming_scope_details.feeder_scope: No conventional source description was substituted for the selected southern start. Generalized cartography does not fix the hydronym of every small initial channel detail.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Duck River and Canje are contextual tributaries, not additional selected pieces or aliases.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Berbice near New Amsterdam and Rosignol; no exact mouth, shoreline or tidal limit assigned.
naming_scope_details.source_authority_limit: WWF institutional field cartography and an explicitly credited Guyana Lands and Surveys Commission national map. Neither is used as a formal hydronym adjudication.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Model mainstem roles and fragment boundaries do not establish official hydronym limits. Modeled length is not official river length. No naming date, historical alias sequence, Indigenous-name equivalence or Korean form is established.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: Only the representative hydronym is listed; contextual river names retain their separate roles.

records.supported_name_scope: Río Quinto is supported for the central and lower named river corridor. The selection additionally follows a northern Río Grande reservoir approach and a southern continuation beyond the continuously mapped Quinto channel in the La Amarga receiving country. No single whole-object hydronym is established.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The north–south upper approach, Antonio Esteban Agüero and La Florida reservoir corridor, Paso de las Carretas, southeast Quinto course across the provincial boundary and La Amarga receiving lowlands distinguish this selection from the Conlara and Desaguadero systems. The initial route is not replaced by the western Trapiche source route.
records.region: Central San Luis and southern Córdoba, Argentina.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded correspondence and naming-scope hold after inspecting the complete selection and readable original regional maps. No further acquisition is pending for this assessment. A future whole-object assignment requires positive evidence for the southern receiving-terrain connection and feature class. The initial feeder's unresolved name is a separate naming limit, not the reason for the hold.

naming_scope_details.supported_named_trunk: Río Quinto; Popopis is retained as the parenthetical name printed on the IGN trunk, not a separately selected component.
naming_scope_details.upper_route: Northern Río Grande reservoir approach through Antonio Esteban Agüero toward La Florida. The first feeder and exact local hydronym transitions remain unassigned; Los Manantiales is a separately reported contributing watercourse, not an alias applied to the whole upper selection.
naming_scope_details.reservoir_roles: Antonio Esteban Agüero, La Florida and Paso de las Carretas are impoundment anchors. Their names do not replace river names. Vulpiani provides lower cartographic context.
naming_scope_details.other_headwater_roles: Trapiche is the separate western source approach described by the federal publication. The nearby La Bajada label is not transferred to the selected northern feeder.
naming_scope_details.terminal_roles: Bañados de la Amarga is the receiving wetland setting; Laguna La Amarga is a distinct mapped waterbody. Neither is asserted to name or contain the entire modeled southern continuation.
naming_scope_details.reason_for_hold: The final connection and feature class are not established across the transition from named river to wetland and southern receiving terrain. Regional-map omission does not prove the terrain is permanently dry or disconnected, but it also cannot justify extending Quinto throughout it.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: One modeled mainstem fragment does not imply one natural river, one hydronym, current hydraulic continuity or an official source-to-mouth length. No precise naming transition, surveyed lake boundary, present inundation, permanent endorheic condition or Korean name is assigned.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: Only the supported representative trunk name is listed. Feeder, reservoir and receiving-wetland names retain separate roles above. The whole-object candidate remains null.
naming_scope_details.completion_scope: Completed bounded correspondence and naming-scope hold after inspecting the complete selection and readable original regional maps. No further acquisition is pending for this assessment. A future whole-object assignment requires positive evidence for the southern receiving-terrain connection and feature class. The initial feeder's unresolved name is a separate naming limit, not the reason for the hold.

records.supported_name_scope: Casas Grandes is the representative receiving-river identity. Peñitas and Palanganas retain distinct upstream roles; Laguna de Guzmán is the receiving inland waterbody, not a river alias. The representative name is not asserted for every selected segment.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The southern Peñitas approach, northwestern turn into Palanganas, Casas Grandes valley, Ascensión reach, large loop north of Sierra Boca Grande and southward approach to Laguna de Guzmán jointly match the selection. The western Piedras Verdes headwaters and eastern Santa María drainage are distinct.
records.region: Northwestern Chihuahua, Mexico, from the Ignacio Zaragoza uplands through Casas Grandes and Ascensión to the Laguna de Guzmán depression.
records.completion_scope: Completed for bounded representative-system identity using the complete selected line and readable primary map pixels. The first small feeder is unnamed. Exact stream-name transition points, individual terminal waterbody components and current water extent are not assigned. The actual inland connection and receiving-lake identity are supported at the reviewed cartographic scale.

naming_scope_details.distinct_selected_upstream_route: Unnamed short southern feeder, then the Peñitas corridor and the Palanganas approach before the Casas Grandes trunk.
naming_scope_details.feeder_scope: Peñitas names a supported part of the southern approach. The first short feeder and exact Peñitas-to-Palanganas naming boundary remain unassigned. San José and Junta de los Arroyos are separately mapped tributary approaches, not alternative names for the whole selected route.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: The complete southern selection was compared with municipal relief pixels. The western Piedras Verdes route is not the selected headwater approach. Neither Palanganas nor Peñitas is presented as an alias for Casas Grandes.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: The receiving inland waterbody is supported as Laguna de Guzmán by the Ascensión relief map. Nearby Laguna Escondida and the southern Chalchihuites/Babícora waters are contextual features, not asserted selected lake passages. Individual components or local labels within the terminal depression are not assigned exact boundaries.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: The selected northern loop and final southward connection reach Laguna de Guzmán. This is an inland terminal setting, not an ocean mouth. No perennial through-flow, current shoreline, exact inlet vertex, complete lake traversal, outlet or onward connector is inferred.
naming_scope_details.nearby_exclusions: Santa María and its receiving lake constitute a separately mapped eastern corridor; the selection is not extended to them. Nearby El Fresnal is not added as a selected terminal or connector.
naming_scope_details.historical_source_scope: The state sheet is fourth edition 2024, copyright 2025, with topographic planimetry derived from sixth-edition 2023 1:250,000 coverage. Municipal compendia date to 2010 and support historical cartographic identity and network context, not present-day water extent or discharge.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Model mainstem status, endpoints and modeled length do not establish official name limits, source location, permanent flow or river length. No formal naming history, alias equivalence or Korean name is established.
naming_scope_details.candidate_names_scope: Only the representative river is included. Feeder, upstream-river and lake names remain in their separate roles above.

records.supported_name_scope: No natural river identity is established for the complete modeled Inland Ice path. This completed feature-class and naming-scope hold does not claim that every nearby marginal stream is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Southeastern Greenland Inland Ice, extending nearly south from the interior before a westward step and a long southern continuation toward the glaciated margin west of the Tasiilaq–Sermilik coastal region. Coastal names are regional context only; no exact terminal natural feature is assigned.
records.completion_scope: Readable coverage supports the completed scope hold. Positive natural-river identity evidence would be required before any later name assignment; no further acquisition is pending now.

naming_scope_details.length_limit: Model display length, not a measured natural-river length.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
